risks.title: Cybersecurity and intrusion risks
risks.score_rationale: Listed first in general risk factors with language indicating ongoing concern despite mitigation efforts. The company has explicitly suffered unauthorized intrusions and cannot eliminate all risks or guarantee that no undetected intrusions have occurred.

risks.title: Litigation and legal proceedings risks
risks.score_rationale: Listed in the general risk factors section, the language covers a wide range of potential litigation including intellectual property matters, contracts, and other claims.

risks.title: Dependence on third-party providers for security
risks.score_rationale: This risk is a direct extension of the cybersecurity risk, specifically focused on third parties. The text explicitly emphasizes that control over and ability to monitor third-party security posture remains limited, and contractual protections may be insufficient.

risks.title: Debt structure and financial obligations risks
risks.score_rationale: The debt section details significant amounts for People Inc.: Term Loan A-1 ($341.3 million), Term Loan B-2 ($700 million), and 2032 Notes ($400 million), indicating exposure to interest rate, refinancing, and repayment risks.

risks.title: Risks related to print operations and distribution
risks.score_rationale: People Inc. maintains a Print segment including magazine subscriptions, newsstand sales, and advertising agency operations, with significant distribution and production costs mentioned in operating expenses.

risks.title: Risks related to digital advertising revenue dependence
risks.score_rationale: A significant portion of People Inc. revenues derives from digital advertising (including D/Cipher+) and performance marketing, highly competitive markets sensitive to algorithmic changes, regulations, and macroeconomic conditions.

ai_positioning.summary: IAC mentions artificial intelligence in the context of People Inc. activities, particularly regarding content licensing for large-language models and related AI activities. Content monetization for AI applications represents a growing opportunity within the company's portfolio.
evidence: Content licensing royalties earned from relationships with Apple News+ and other content use and distribution relationships, including utilization in large-language models and other artificial intelligence (AI) related activities
